newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable but listless amid thin talks.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Stable but listless amid thin talks.

text.p: A lack of physical activities plus a weekend mood kept the high sulphur fuel oil market listless and prices stable on Friday, traders said.
A major was heard to sell a 20,000-tonne cargo of 180-cst grade for lifting April 6-10 at $98 per tonne.
Early in the week, suppliers offered the 180-cst grade at $98-$101 per tonne but could not find buyers.
"The market is generally very quiet and not much is happening," said one trader.
Most traders were searching for a clear market direction after a week of quiet trade, reluctant to take action.

"Demand from China is there with the approach of the summer time and the harvest season, but you have to note one important factor that Korean supplies are better for China in terms of quality and prices," said one Chinese trader.
On Friday, Taiwan's state-run Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) sold three 30,000-tonne cargoes of 3.0-percent high sulphur fuel oil at below $100 per tonne for April 8-26 lifting.
The price was lower than $103 per tonne when it last sold three cargoes at $103 per tonne for March lifting.
In the swaps market, March were last quoted at $98.00/$99.00 per tonne and April were at $97.00/$98.00, little changed from Thursday's $98.50/$99.50 and $96.50/$97.25 respectively.
Despite the lacklustre trade interest and no signs of major gains in prices, traders agreed that levels should be well supported in the near term.
Traders were not worried by the high stock build in Singapore weekly residue stocks of 12.692 million barrels in the week ending March 12, the highest volume since early May 1996.
"It's been expected," said one trader.
Several maintenance turnarounds in this region, though not expected to take the length out of stocks significantly, should be able to support sentiment, they said.
Recent strength in crude values would also help support prices, they added.
In the LSWR market, the Korean Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) issued a tender to buy 500,000 barrels of May LSWR for delivery between May 11-15 to the ports of Ulsan and Pusan.
The tender closes March 19 and is valid for one day.
